headline: Mostly light, spotty rain chances Sunday and again Tuesday night into Wednesday give way to a sunny, warm Thanksgiving and Black Friday (Friday about 10 degrees above normal), but forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding and big surf during Thanksgiving week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A weak front moves through Sunday, most likely bringing light rain to the Central Coast this afternoon, with a smaller chance for Los Angeles County and areas around Glendale and the rest of the region south of Point Conception. Most places south of Point Conception get only a trace to 0.05 inch, possibly up to a tenth, while the Central Coast gets about a tenth (no more than a quarter inch); a chance of light rain lingers Sunday night. Temperatures change little, with highs in the mid to upper 60s across the coasts and valleys and a few 70-degree readings in the San Gabriel Valley.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Monday looks very nice, with mostly sunny skies, a light breeze off the land, and highs up a degree or two but still a couple of degrees below normal. Tuesday brings partly cloudy skies (mostly cloudy on the Central Coast in the afternoon) and highs 2 to 4 degrees warmer, in the upper 60s to lower 70s across most coasts and valleys, with offshore winds not strong enough to cause problems. Tuesday night turns mostly cloudy as the next storm approaches, with rain likely in coastal San Luis Obispo County and a 40 percent chance reaching western Santa Barbara County by dawn Wednesday; amounts stay under a tenth of an inch except up to a quarter inch on the northwest tip of San Luis Obispo County.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The storm moves through quickly Wednesday morning and falls apart, giving the Central Coast a 20 to 30 percent chance of light rain (under a tenth of an inch) and Los Angeles and Ventura counties less than a 10 percent chance, then skies clear and highs warm 1 to 3 degrees in the afternoon. Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday look spectacular as strong high pressure builds in with offshore winds: expect sunny skies and locally breezy mornings, with 3 to 6 degrees of warming Thanksgiving and another 2 to 4 degrees Friday, when highs reach the mid 70s to low 80s, about 10 degrees above normal; there is only a low chance of advisory-level wind gusts Friday. A fast-moving disturbance brings a 20 to 30 percent chance of light rain, mainly to the Central Coast (under a tenth of an inch), on Saturday, while winds turning onshore and more clouds cool highs by about 5 degrees.

coast: Forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding during Thanksgiving week, from a combination of unusually high sea levels (warm ocean water expands), very high spring tides and a large, long-period west swell. For the Central Coast, Ventura and Los Angeles county beaches, a Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM Wednesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon as the swell arrives; peak high tides come between 8:45 and 10 AM at roughly 8.2–8.4 feet for Los Angeles and Ventura and 7.9–8.2 feet on the Central Coast, with a reasonable worst case 0.3–0.5 feet higher, and significant impacts seem probable. If upgraded to a warning, flooding could reach farther inland and damage coastal roads and buildings, with significant beach erosion; areas of greatest concern include Santa Monica to Palos Verdes, Long Beach/Naples, Faria to Silver Strand Beach including Ventura Harbor, and Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes and the Cayucos, Avila and Pismo piers. A High Surf Advisory covers the Central Coast from 6 AM Sunday to 3 PM Thursday: surf up to 11 feet Monday morning, a lull Monday night into Tuesday, then rapid building to 10–15 feet Wednesday morning and 15–20 feet Wednesday afternoon and evening, possibly higher, with an upgrade to a High Surf Warning increasingly likely, probably by Tuesday. Ventura and Los Angeles county beaches see elevated to high surf much of the week, peaking Wednesday and Thursday with likely High Surf Advisories and a small chance of warning-level surf up to 15 feet on the Ventura coast. The Santa Barbara South Coast (Santa Barbara to Rincon and Jalama Beach) and the islands are under a Coastal Flood Advisory from 3 AM Monday to 3 PM Thursday, with more coastal alerts likely Friday. Offshore, winds and seas stay below small craft advisory levels through Tuesday; a significant west swell around 14–16 feet arrives midweek with large, hazardous seas on the outer waters, and two storms (Sunday into Sunday night, and Wednesday) bring the best rain chances to the waters north of Point Conception, and low-end advisory-level northwest to west winds are possible Wednesday and Wednesday night south of Point Conception. Officials advise staying off the beach and away from rock jetties, and avoiding flooded roads and walkways.
watch_for: Coastal flooding and high surf Thanksgiving week: Coastal Flood Watch late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon for Los Angeles, Ventura and Central Coast beaches, with a possible upgrade to warnings.
Light rain chances Sunday and again Tuesday night into Wednesday, mostly on the Central Coast.
How breezy the offshore winds get on the warm Thanksgiving and Black Friday mornings (low chance of advisory-level gusts).
confidence: Forecasters are confident in mostly light rain amounts and a dry, warm Thanksgiving and Black Friday, while there is still some uncertainty about exactly how the high tides and big midweek swell will line up, though significant coastal impacts seem probable.
